issues.detail: Hebrew 'אִבְחַת חָרֶב' means 'the slaughter of the sword' or 'the flashing of the sword' (a sword's edge/glint), not '刀劍的亞比加' (the 'Abiga' of the sword). 'אִבְחַת' is a noun meaning 'slaughter' or 'flash/glint', not a proper name. The Chinese adds a transliterated name '亞比加' that has no basis in the Hebrew.

Hebrew 'מְעֻטָּה לְטָבַח' means 'wrapped/polished for slaughter' (i.e., the sword is prepared for killing), not '作閃電中微少的祭物' ('as a small sacrifice in the lightning'). 'מְעֻטָּה' is a passive participle meaning 'wrapped' or 'polished', and 'לְטָבַח' means 'for slaughter', not 'a small sacrifice'.
